brief.situation: You are the Azure Virtual Desktop administrator at Merrow Insurance, a fictional insurer. The claims call center (300 agents) works on the hp-claims host pool, whose egress goes through Azure Firewall Premium in the hub. Overnight the security team enabled TLS inspection on the firewall's application rules for the AVD spoke. Since 05:40 every session host shows Unavailable. The day shift logs on at 08:00.
handover: The security team's change ticket says inspection must stay on for general web traffic from the spoke.
Session hosts' egress: route 0.0.0.0/0 to the firewall's private IP.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the session hosts, the hub firewall with its new TLS inspection and the AVD service they must reach.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the hosts went Unavailable, what you changed, and why not simply bypass the firewall.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Connects a shared failure to the shared change.
parts.modelAnswer: All 40 hosts stopped heartbeating at 05:40, five minutes after TLS inspection was enabled. The firewall logs showed the broker traffic inspected and the agent rejected the firewall's certificate.

parts.label: Change
parts.criteria: Narrow exclusion as the guidance says.
parts.modelAnswer: A route for the WindowsVirtualDesktop service tag to Internet and the AVD FQDN tag excluded from inspection. Web traffic from the spoke is still inspected.

parts.label: Not bypass
parts.modelAnswer: Deleting the default route would have removed inspection and logging for all of the call center's traffic. The exclusion was agreed with security and an alert watches host health.

expertPath.text: All hosts Unavailable since 05:40; broker traffic TLS-inspected since 05:35; agent rejects the firewall CA; all traffic via the firewall.
Service-tag route to Internet; AVD FQDN tag excluded from inspection; agreed with security; heartbeat alert.

uninspected.headline: Exempt the service, not the network
uninspected.body: Only AVD's own service traffic must avoid TLS inspection. A service-tag route and an exclusion for the FQDN tag keep everything else inspected.

shiftDown.headline: Inspection broke the agent's connection
shiftDown.body: AVD's agent and service connections must not be TLS-inspected. Exclude the WindowsVirtualDesktop traffic and route its service tag directly.

excluded.headline: Good: troubleshot the path, kept the control
excluded.body: You saw all hosts fail together, found the inspected broker traffic in the firewall logs, excluded only the AVD service traffic as the vendor guidance says, checked a sign-in, and made the exclusion part of the security change.

gaps.headline: Held, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the evidence before the change, the lasting step, the check, or the cause in the record.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: All hosts failed at once, right after TLS inspection was turned on, and the firewall logs show their broker connections being inspected while the agent rejects the firewall's certificate. AVD guidance says not to TLS-inspect its traffic: route the WindowsVirtualDesktop service tag directly and exclude the AVD FQDN tag from inspection, leaving everything else inspected. Removing the default route bypasses the firewall entirely; restarting hosts changes nothing. Agree the exclusion with security and alert on host health.
